messages:
priya: Canary alert earlier shows 'x-api-key' header being logged by runtime when upstream error occurred. snippet:
```
[2026-11-02T09:12:23Z] ERROR request_id=abc123 headers={"authorization":"Bearer sk_live_ABC...","x-api-key":"cust-789"}
```

sam: :rotating_light: thanks. which env? prod or staging?

kevin: prod canary - small percent. I can grep S3 logs and app logs, but need permission to pull customer ids.

anya: I checked - the canary request was from dedicated bucket for canary traffic (customer-id: cust-789). It looks like x-api-key contains a non-sensitive internal key but authorization header was redacted in some logs, not this one.

priya: initial ask: scope exposure (which headers persisted to long-term logs), and confirm who accessed those logs since 09:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Log access audit: user_access: sam, anya, dave-sre; ip: 35.204.12.4, 52.14.7.21; show further details in /audit/1805123456

sam: I'll run a grep across the last 24h and list objects. assigning to me.

kevin: I'll prepare a hotfix to strip x-* headers before writing to logs, and open a PR. ETA 45m.

anya: Legal/PR check: do we need to notify the affected customer? tagging laura-legal for advice.

laura-legal: please confirm: full tokens exposed, or pseudonymized keys? if it's internal test key and not customer PII, may need internal comms only. need list of affected accounts + whether keys are usable.

priya: From quick look, the value is cust-789 which maps to a test tenant used in canary; token looks like a short key 'cust-789' not bearer token. but authorization header contained bearer token earlier in other logs — unclear if full tokens persisted elsewhere.

sam: grep results: 3 objects in /prod/runtime-logs/2026-11-02 with x-api-key entries. Objects retrieved by dave-sre and sam. No other accessers in 24h.

kevin: PR opened: github.com/redwood/plat/commit/abcdef - removes header logging and adds redaction util. rolling canary now paused. :white_check_mark: 

priya: can we redact the stored objects? who can rewrite S3 logs? we should rotate keys if any real tokens found.

anya: S3 rewrite requires infra write access; dave-sre can run a scrub job. I'll schedule it.

dave-sre: I can run scrub job now, will redact x-api-key values and replace with [REDACTED], will record S3 object versions. starting.

priya: tagging customer comms: we should draft a short internal note first. laura-legal: do we need to send external notice if only test tenant affected?

laura-legal: if only canary/test tenant, internal comms only. but if any bearer tokens persisted and those tokens could be used to access customer data, we must notify. please provide confirmation by EOD UTC.

sam: confirmed no bearer tokens in these 3 objects. we ran additional grep across all runtime logs and found zero matches for 'Bearer sk_' pattern alongside x-api-key. searching full logs now.

priya: action items: (1) kevin's PR live to all regions (after review), (2) dave scrub job complete + S3 versions recorded, (3) sam final grep across all logs + list of obj ids, (4) laura provide comms guidance. I'll create an incident Jira and link.

priya: Jira created: RW-INC-2026-321 (internal-only). I'll update with artifacts.

kevin: once scrub done, let's rotate any keys used in canary infra.

dave-sre: scrub finished, replaced values, recorded versions: v1->v2. added note to Jira. no external access detected.

priya: thanks everyone. closing loop: we will not notify external customers per legal. keep thread for any follow-ups.

anya: adding retrospective note to postmortem template.

sam: thumbs up :thumbsup: 

priya: filing follow-up RFC for stricter header logging guardrails.
